ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: visitors on the map
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: The rider, the family or the envoy a letter speaks of waits at the gate while you decide; guests stay their night, and herds and mourners pass on the road.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Keep the way from the map's edge to the gate open and the gate clear: someone who can't get there, or can't stand the weather by it, goes home, and the letter alone tells it.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description:
With "Goods and people come and go on the map" on (the Events and world page of the settings, on by default), the people Rimfolk's world events speak of are on the map. When a letter says a rider is waiting at the gate for the colony's answer, the rider walks in from the edge with it and stands by the gate until you answer, or until the letter runs out. A family asking to be taken in waits there with their children and their dog. Take them in and those are the people who join, right where they stand.
What you send goes out to them by hand: a colonist carries the medicine or the sack of food to the rider at the gate, and what their people pay, they set down there themselves. A smith or a merchant house's agent who buys from you takes the goods from your hands and pays on the spot. Guests given a night sleep by the gate, or under your roof when the answer gave them a bed, and go on at first light, and pilgrims or prospectors you let stay camp by water out on your land, clear of the colony. Mourners, a clan's band or a lord's progress pass along the road outside the colony and go on to the far side of the map, and drovers bring their herd onto the far meadow for the night, or down to the water.

li.heading: Who comes

table.li: A plague, a famine, a hard winter, a flood, a fire, a drought, a good harvest, rebuilding after a war | A rider, or a driver with a beast from their carts | Waits at the gate for your answer. What you send goes out to them (for a cartload of timber or food, to the porters who come for it), and what their people pay they set down there
Iron gone scarce, a merchant house on a reopened road | A smith with his cart, or the house's agent | Waits at the gate. What you sell is carried out to them, and they pay for it then and there

Refugees, exiles, a burned-out family, a freed captive, a survivor, a deserter, a prospector who has given up, a girl left at the gate by a famine, a failed merchant house's unpaid driver | The family or the person asking | Taken in, they join where they stand. Fed and sent on, a family sleeps by the wall and goes at first light, and someone alone goes on soon after

A new town, a levy, a vote, a new road, the road's guards, envoys, a herald, a patrol, salvagers, two drovers with a heifer, the road gang's foreman, the toll-keeper's man, the riders of two claimants | One to three of them | Wait at the gate for the answer, then go home

A blood feud | The young man running from it, later an elder of the other family | The runaway waits at the gate (hidden, he stays two nights), and a rider of the other family goes by on the road soon after he comes. The elder waits for the blood price, and it is carried out to him

Pilgrims asking alms, families walking home, hunters asking leave, pilgrims stopping for a blessing on their way home | A line of three to five of them | Wait for your answer, take what you send, and go on past the colony

Pilgrims asking to camp, prospectors asking to work the creeks | Three to five pilgrims, two or three prospectors | Let stay, they camp by water clear of the colony for three nights and go on. The prospectors pan the creek from morning into the evening, and the pilgrims sing at their camp after dark. Prospectors who strike color come back to work the creek by lamplight for a night

Drovers, herders in a drought | One asks at the gate. Then two or three come with five to eight head | The herd grazes the far meadow, or drinks at the water, overnight and goes on at first light. Drovers welcomed as friends come up to the colony's fire for the evening
Mourners, a clan's band, a lord's progress | Four to six, with a beast or horses | Pass along the road outside the colony and go on to the far side of the map

Snowbound travelers, a robbed merchant, a singer, a stargazer | One or two guests | Stay their nights (two for the travelers, three for the stargazer, on the far ground) and go on at first light. The travelers and the singer sleep under your roof, the singer comes to the evening's fire, and whoever sits up with the stargazer goes out to her hill the first night
A feud's warning, a debt come due, a runaway mule's owner (the last two in a colony of the old ways) | A rider | Waits at the gate while you decide

A prophet on the roads | Three of her followers, later the prophet herself | The followers wait for your answer and take the bread, or sleep by the wall. Let the prophet speak and she stays the night, and those who want to hear her gather round her at the gate at dusk

An old vault, a failing merchant house, closed markets, gleaners after a bumper harvest, a toll | A scavenger or a bailiff with a cart, the house's old master, a carter or a smuggler of the shut-out people, three gleaners, a carter dodging the toll | Wait at the gate. What you buy they set down, a loan is carried out to the old master, and gleaners you let in go over your stubble by day and sleep on the far ground

The ice road | The road-keeper with his sledge, a soaked driver, a caravan's leader | Wait at the gate. The driver thaws indoors overnight while his load is pulled out of the shallows, and a caravan given the barn beds down in it with its beasts

A moot of the peoples, an old thrumbo | The moot's herald and three delegates, two horn hunters of another people, an elder | Wait at the gate. Delegates you put up eat what is carried out to them and stay the night

A beat that follows an earlier answer | The hidden boy's mother, a tinker, a rider with a stargazer's notes or a keepsake, the burned town's carter with boards, a smith with new iron, drovers on their way home | Hand over what they brought at the gate and go home

li.text: A lord's retinue that you host comes in the evening and stays the night by the gate, and the letter about their stay comes after they've gone. Not every letter's people come: those at war with the colony (a warlord's rider, a deserter's old unit), two peoples at war with each other, and people a world event keeps for later stay in the letter.

li.heading: When they don't come, and when they go early
li.text:
They come only from a people at peace with the colony, and only when the map is safe: no raiders, no bitter cold or heat, nothing in the air. At most three groups of them are on the map at once, each of at most six people and eight animals. If they can't come, or the setting is off, the letter tells it as before, and what you send is fetched by a courier instead (see "goods carried by hand").
Hurt or arrest one of them, or let their people turn hostile, and they leave at once, defending themselves. If raiders come they leave at a jog. If the cold, the heat or hunger starts to get to them they go on, and a message says so. Someone at the gate waits two and a half days at most, and goes about half an hour after you answer, or once what you send has reached them. Guests sleep by the gate, or, when the answer gave them a bed or a roof or a night out would hurt them, in a corner of your dining room or rec room (a barn first, for a caravan given the barn; they keep to it); with no warm room to offer, they go on, and a message says so. It all saves with the game, and a visit cut short by a reload or a lost map simply ends.

li.heading: Their own way
li.text: Visitors eat what they brought and sleep when they're tired or night comes, on open ground near their spot. Out of doors they never go into your rooms or onto your fields, and they take nothing; a herd on the far meadow doesn't touch your fields either. Those who came to do something do it: prospectors pan the creek, gleaners go over the stubble, pilgrims sing after dark, and the other settlers' hunters walk the far side watching for game. Their animals rest close by. What the colony hands them goes with them. Now and then one of them says a line: on arriving, while waiting, when given the night, when passing, and when leaving.

li.heading: Faces that come back
li.text: Some visitors the colony keeps up with: the tinker, the scholar, the doctor with the inoculations, the schoolteacher, the bonesetter, the wandering cook, the scribe, the players' storyteller and the kindred spirit. When their visit ends they are remembered, up to five of them at a time, with the colonist they dealt with first. From twenty days after their visit, one of them may come back ("a familiar face at the gate"): the same person, asking after that colonist, with a lesson in their trade to give for a welcome. Welcome them and the thread between you deepens; turn them away and it frays; someone not seen for half a year is forgotten, as is anyone whose people turn against the colony. On their third visit or later, when the thread holds (three warm visits at least), it turns: they ask the council for a place here for good, or ask their friend to come with them and see the road for a season or two. Either answer plays out as the words say: they join, or the colonist packs and leaves with them when the visit ends. The World page lists them under "Out there" with how many times they have come.

li.heading: What visitors notice
li.text: A visitor at the gate, or a guest staying with Hospitality, looks around. If the colony has something worth remarking on they say so, once per thing seen: a great hall (an impressive room of some size), art of excellent quality or better, three graves or more, a shrine, walls with turrets or a long run of wall, many animals near the yard, or wide fields. Word spreads: when enough visitors have remarked on the halls, the art, the graves or the walls, the colony is known for them, as one of four colony traits (famed hall, artful, hallowed, walled; see "the colony's character"), and the events those draw come more often: the tourists, the celebrity and the players to a famed hall, the pilgrims to a hallowed one, scholars and scribes to the art. "Travellers speak of..." on the World page under "Out there" says what the colony is known for.

li.heading: Guests in the colony's stories (Hospitality)
li.text: With Hospitality, a guest already staying can be the stranger a story is about, about half the time when one of the guests fits (grown, up and about, their people at peace with the colony, the right age for the story). The old flame can be someone at the guest beds who turns out to have known a colonist long ago; the one who asks to learn a trade, the tinker or the teller who becomes a regular, likewise. Such a guest doesn't wait at the edge of the map; the story finds them where they are. An answer that has them join hands them over through Hospitality's own joining, so their people are told the same way, and an answer that sends strangers away leaves a guest to Hospitality's own rules. The setting "Guests in the colony's stories" (Guests page of the mod settings) turns it off, and stories bring their own strangers as before.
